children: Asian equities fell on Wednesday November 25, after a fresh sell-off in US technology shares seemed to have reignited doubts over how long the artificial intelligence (AI) rally can last.

Kospi led the retreat, dropping 4.81%, while Taiex lost 3.77% and the Nikkei 225 shed 2.72%. Topix slipped 0.38%, but Hang Seng edged up 0.15%, and its futures gained 0.7%. The MSCI Asia Pacific Index slipped 0.6%, a day after its biggest rally since July.
In India, GIFT Nifty pointed to a positive start. Analysts see 25,500 as the first upside level for the Nifty, with support at 25,167.
Among regional currencies, the Japanese yen was little changed at 159.28 per dollar, while the offshore yuan remained close to 6.6655 per dollar.
Wall Street set the tone for the early market movement. The Nasdaq 100 lost 2% overnight, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 7.9%, leaving it 40% below its June peak.

The Nasdaq composite closed 1.5% lower after rebounding more than 7% the session before, and the S&P 500 fell 0.5%. The Dow Jones bucked the trend, adding 425 points to climb back above 50,000. Dell and HP rose in extended trading after issuing upbeat forecasts.

Chipmakers took the heaviest blows. Nvidia sank 6.5%, handing back part of the 31% surge that followed Jensen Huang's return as chief executive. President Donald Trump claimed credit for that comeback. "I spoke to 'em. Let me just put it that way, and I convinced 'em... I made the deal," he told CNBC.
Huang still faces congressional hearings, and investigations into the company will continue from December 1. Anthropic fell 6.5%, wiping out its post-IPO gains and closing below its listing price.

Several pressures weighed on sentiment. Investors question whether huge technology spending can justify elevated valuations. Bloomberg reported that Washington could announce higher tariffs on China, the European Union and more than a dozen other economies as soon as Tuesday.

Sources cited by Bloomberg said the new levies would not lift overall rates above those agreed in existing trade deals. Traders also awaited the Personal Consumption Expenditure inflation reading, the Federal Reserve's preferred gauge, which may strengthen bets on a December rate rise after US consumer confidence hit a near two-year high.

US Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh meanwhile called AI a "hinge" of history and describes himself as "cautiously optimistic" about it, but officials still debate whether it will transform the economy, fuel inflation or trigger a downturn.
On the commodity side, oil slipped in early Asian trade as traders weighed signs of growing supply against a run of attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent crude fell to $90.96 a barrel after closing above $91 on Monday, while West Texas Intermediate for January delivery dropped 0.5% to $81.65 after a 2.4% gain in the previous session.

title: Kospi slumps nearly 5%; Asian markets fall after US tech sell-off sparks AI rally doubts
